set.body:
recall/graph.scala:12 declares `final case class RecallGraph(` -- a fully PUBLIC case class. No
private constructor, no smart constructor, no phantom witness. And graph.scala:34 is
`def validated(g: RecallGraph): ValidatedNec[DomainError, RecallGraph]` -- it takes the type and
returns THE SAME TYPE.

So validation here is ADVISORY, not binding. A validated RecallGraph is indistinguishable, at
the type level, from one nobody ever checked. Six direct `RecallGraph(...)` constructions exist
in main sources and none of them is required to pass through validated at all.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR WORK THAT LANDED TODAY. m1's 4383a85 added the text-must-be-the-words-at-its
-span law inside validated(). I verified that fix and closed two beads on it
(bd-01M16KE05GFKF1JW3HCMAQVDSS, bd-01M16KGSC33Z59JZNMBRBJF659). The law is correctly
implemented and it is not enforceable: anyone can build a violating graph directly, or take a
validated one and copy() it into a violating one.

That is not hypothetical. codec/AlignCodecSuite.scala:38-42 does exactly this, today, on main:

  val changed = fixture.recall.copy(units =
    fixture.recall.units.map(unit =>
      if unit.id == first.id then unit.copy(text = unit.text + " changed") else unit))

That test is CORRECT and should not change -- it deliberately builds an incoherent graph to
prove the codec rejects it on recallChecksum, and it still fails for that reason since it never
calls validated. I am citing it only as proof that the bypass is one line and already in use.

REQUIRED: give RecallGraph a real construction boundary. Either a private constructor with a
smart constructor returning a witness-carrying type, or a phantom status parameter in the shape
of AmrGraph[C <: CheckState] / StoryModel[S <: ModelStatus], both of which slice 7 made
unforgeable. Whichever shape, validated must stop returning its own input type -- that signature
is the defect in miniature.

WHY THE SWEEP MISSED IT, which is the part worth generalising and is on the parent bead
bd-01M1697234KP2X44X6Q8S6C6Y7: the fromProduct sweep enumerated PRIVATE-CONSTRUCTOR case classes
-- types that were TRYING to be boundaries and failing. RecallGraph never tried, so it never
appeared in any slice's scope. A sweep for defeated boundaries cannot find a missing one.

Coordinate with m1, who owns the text-at-span law and whose work this makes binding.
set.title: recall: RecallGraph is a public case class and validated() returns its own input type, so the text-at-span law is advisory
